@graph.headline: What is an SOP, and when does a small business need one?
@graph.description: What an SOP is, what it is not, and the one sign a 10 to 20 person business needs one. A plain guide from Nuvato AI.
@graph.abstract: An SOP is a standard operating procedure. It is a written description of how one job in your business gets done, step by step, so the result does not depend on who does it.

acceptedAnswer.text: An SOP covers one job. How an invoice gets sent. How a new customer is set up. How a service call is closed out. How a quote is checked before it leaves the building.
It is not a policy manual. A policy says what the business believes. An SOP says what to do on Tuesday.

mainEntity.name: How do you know a small business needs an SOP?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is one sign that matters most. Someone is holding the process in their head.

mainEntity.name: What does a good SOP contain?

acceptedAnswer.text: A good SOP is short enough to be read while doing the job. It has the same parts every time, so people know where to look.

mainEntity.name: Which process should you write down first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pick the one that has all three of these traits. It repeats. It causes mistakes or delays when it goes wrong. And it depends on one person.

mainEntity.name: How do you keep an SOP from going stale?

acceptedAnswer.text: Give it an owner and a review date. Those two things do the work.
